turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I… I shall, ma’am. But… but I’m not quite certain which door, you see. It’s all rather… very confusing, isn’t it?

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Confusing, is it? Yes, yes, everything is… everything *was* so carefully arranged, you see. Such precise placement, such deliberate disorder… but time, time has a way of… of rearranging, does it not?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Indeed, ma’am. Time… it is a most unsettling thing, to observe its effects. I… I suppose it would be quite disorienting to witness such a… a shifting of order, wouldn’t it?

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Disorienting, you say? Yes, quite. It is… it is like a tapestry, unraveling thread by thread, the pattern lost, the colours fading… and I, I remain, a solitary figure amidst the ruins of what *was*. Come closer, Pip; do you see it? The unraveling?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I… I do see it, ma’am. It is… it is rather striking, the way the light catches the dust, and… and shows the… the looseness, you understand. It’s… it’s quite remarkable, really.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Remarkable, you say? Yes, remarkable, though I scarcely notice it anymore. The dust… the looseness… it is all part of the stillness, you see. Stillness… a most profound stillness, which I find… agreeable, in its way.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: It… it is, ma’am. A stillness… yes, I comprehend. It is… it is rather pervasive, isn't it? I… I find myself quite struck by the… the quietude of it all.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Quietude, you say? Yes, quietude… a silence so complete, it echoes. It is the silence of a vow broken, Pip… a silence that weighs upon me, a perpetual, crushing… weight. Come nearer, child; feel it with me, this stillness.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Indeed, ma’am. A… a crushing weight, you say? I… I can almost imagine it, though I… I confess, I am not entirely certain how one would… how one would truly *feel* such a thing. It is… it is a most solemn observation, ma’am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Solemn, you say? Yes, solemn… a word laden with meaning, Pip, a meaning I have learned to… to savor, in a way. Tell me, child, do you *understand* solemn? Do you understand the… the utter finality of a promise unfulfilled?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I… I believe I do, ma’am, in a manner of speaking. Solemnity… it is akin to… to a great and weighty secret, isn’t it? Something one… one observes with a certain… a certain gravity, ma’am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: A secret, Pip? Yes, a secret… and secrets, my dear boy, often fester. They poison the very air we breathe, don't they? Tell me, what secrets do *you* keep, child?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I… I do not keep secrets, ma’am, not really. Only… only the sort of things a boy might, you understand—small observations, perhaps, or… or a fondness for a particular piece of pastry. Nothing… nothing of the grave importance you seem to imply, ma’am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Pastry, you say? A fondness for pastry… a fleeting pleasure, Pip, easily consumed, easily forgotten. But a promise… a promise lingers, doesn’t it? It clings to the very fabric of existence, a relentless… a relentless reminder.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Oh, a promise, ma’am. Yes, I… I can imagine it being like that. Like a… a stone, perhaps? One that sits… sits very still, and… and weighs upon the heart, ma’am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: A stone, Pip? A most apt comparison, my dear boy. But a stone, you see, can be moved, can be cast aside… whereas a promise, a broken promise, remains… remains precisely where it is placed, a monument to what *might* have been. Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I… I strive to be truthful, ma’am, truly I do. But sometimes, I suppose, words find a way to… to twist themselves, even before they leave my lips. It is not a deliberate thing, ma’am, I assure you.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Twist themselves, you say? A most curious observation, Pip. Words, like shadows, are ever shifting, ever deceiving… and so easily manipulated, wouldn't you agree? Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: It is… it is unsettling, ma’am, the way shadows move here. They… they seem to have a life of their own, you see. I… I endeavor to understand, ma’am, but it’s all rather… quite overwhelming.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Overwhelming, is it? Yes, I imagine it is, my dear boy. I, too, once found this house… overwhelming. Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there! play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: So new to him, so old to me; so strange to him, so familiar to me; so melancholy to both of us! Call Estella.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: You can do that. Call Estella. At the door.
